reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset and Brown treat Luke's account as Jesus's only Nazareth visit, against the majority-harmonist view that Matthew and Mark record a later, separate visit.

discrepancy.note: Strauss concludes Luke relocated the Nazareth episode, since its Capernaum references only make sense at the later Matthew/Mark date.

quotes.text: From this, it is plain that the later chronological position of the narrative is the original one, and that Luke, in placing it earlier, out of mere conjecture, was honest or careless enough to retain the mention of the wonders at Capernaum, though only consistent with the later position.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, §58 (1846), on Matthew 13:54 and Luke 4:16.

sides.snippet: Coming into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished
sides.verseText: Coming into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished, and said, \"Where did this man get this wisdom, and these mighty works?

sides.snippet: He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. He entered, as was his custom, into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood up to read.
sides.verseText: He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. He entered, as was his custom, into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood up to read.
